info.title: Go1 API
info.description: Go1 REST API, version 2025-01-01, as published in the Go1 developer API reference. Every path operation is the provider's own OpenAPI operation object, copied verbatim from the endpoints data embedded in each reference page (__NEXT_DATA__ pageProps.endpoints) on developers.go1.com. The info, servers and securitySchemes envelope is assembled from the reference overview (base URL https://gateway.go1.com, Api-Version header) and the OAuth 2.0 grant guides (auth.go1.com token/authorize URLs); scope descriptions are left blank because the operations name scopes without describing them.

tags.name: Categories
tags.description:
The Categories resource provides a structured taxonomy for organizing
and discovering content within Go1. Categories can be applied to
various resource types and support hierarchical relationships to
create intuitive navigation and filtering experiences.

This API allows you to retrieve category information from a portal.
Use this endpoint to build navigation, filtering, and discovery
features that align with your portal's content structure.

**Important notes:**
- Categories are read-only via the API (creation/modification not
supported)
- Category structures may evolve over time—handle missing categories
gracefully in your implementation

tags.name: Collections
tags.description: Collections provide a means to curate learning objects into subset groups. Currently, our system only supports a primary collection known as the `Library` collection. This collection is designed specifically for the management of customer-specific content libraries. Admins leverage the Library collection to seamlessly add, remove, and synchronize content within the Library, ensuring seamless integration with external systems.

tags.name: Compliance
tags.description:
The Compliance resource provides read-only access to compliance
regulations and their linked obligations. Use this endpoint to
discover active compliance taxonomy records by industry, mandate
status, location, and optional topic relationships.

**Important notes:**
- Only active regulations are returned
- Embedded obligations are limited to active obligations
- Topic relationships are included only when requested with
include[]=topics

tags.name: Enrollments
tags.description:
Enrollments represent the record of a user's learning activity within a learning object. An enrollment occurs when a user begins or is assigned a learning object.

The enrollment object contains information about a user's progress through a learning object, such as their enrollment status (not-started, in-progress, completed), the enrollment due date, start date, end date and the enrollment results.

You can use this resource to create, look up and manage enrollments against users and learning objects.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: The File Upload endpoint allows users to upload and manage learning media within the Go1 ecosystem, including images, videos, audio files, documents, and SCORM packages. Uploaded files are securely stored and can be used for playback, embedding, or reference within learning content. Use this resource to upload new files, retrieve file details, and manage media assets for seamless content delivery.

tags.name: Learning objects
tags.description: Learning objects represent learning content that can be consumed by learners within the Go1 ecosystem, for example, a course, document or video. A learning object contains contextual information about the content resource, such as its title, description, thumbnail image, learning outcomes and provider. Use this resource to create, look up and manage learning objects.

tags.name: Plans
tags.description:
The Plans resource represents a customer's subscription plan to Go1, containing details such as the customer’s product tier, term duration, and license count. It manages customer access to Go1 products and facilitates the customer lifecycle, such as transitions between plan upgrades, downgrades, and renewals. 

The Plans API allows Go1 partners who provision and distribute Go1 products to their customer Portals, to create, retrieve, update, and manage plans for their customers. It is essential for the provisioning and management of a customer's access to Go1.

tags.name: Play links
tags.description:
Play links are the means by which a user is granted access to play learning content within the Go1 Player, a Go1-hosted UI for playing learning objects. A play link consists of a URL that when loaded, will log a user into the player to access and play a learning object.

For security reasons, sessions are short-lived and will expire if the customer does not visit the URL. Create sessions on-demand when users intend to play some Go1 content.

tags.name: Playlists
tags.description:
Playlists are a simple way to group learning objects into organised themes of choice, for instance, based on topics or learning outcomes. Playlists enable the larger Go1 content library to be curated into smaller lists of content for review, or to provide inspiration for learners to decide what to learn next.

Use this resource to retrieve the contents of playlists, create a new playlist, and add or remove learning objects from existing playlists.

tags.name: Portals
tags.description:
The Portals resource serves as a dedicated workspace or tenant within Go1. Each portal represents a unique customer's business entity and encapsulates their access to Go1's platform and services. The Portals resource provides detailed information about the associated company, including its settings and configuration.

The Portals API allows Go1 partners who provision and distribute Go1 products to their customers to create, retrieve, update, and manage their customer portals. The Portals API should be used in conjunction with the Plan API for the provisioning and management of a customer's access to Go1.

tags.name: Restrictions
tags.description: The Restrictions service provides APIs for managing restrictions on learning objects, including access control and visibility settings.

tags.name: SCIM
tags.description: The SCIM protocol is an application-level REST protocol for provisioning and managing identity data on the web. The protocol supports creation, discovery, retrieval, and modification of core identity resources.

tags.name: User accounts
tags.description:
The user accounts resource represents a user with access to a Go1 portal. The user account object contains basic contact information about the user and allows you to keep track of the learning activity that is connected to the user through using the enrollment APIs.

Users may have different roles within Go1, such as learner, manager or administrator, that allow different levels of access, see [user roles and permissions](https://intercom.help/go1/en/articles/1703818-user-roles-and-permissions-defined) to learn more.

Use this resource to create, look up and manage user accounts.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Webhooks can be configured via the API to notify your application when a notable events take place in your Go1 portal or your connected customer portals, for example when an enrollment occurs, or when a user is updated. Events are sent to an endpoint URL that is specified by you when creating a new webhook.

Use this resource to create, retrieve and update webhooks. For a list of webhook events, including more information about each event, see the Webhook events resource section.

get.description:
Regulations are canonical Go1 compliance taxonomy records for named laws, regulations, directives, standards, or official frameworks that define or inform organizational compliance expectations. A regulation includes contextual information such as its name, description, citation, enforcing agency, locations, applicable industries, and associated learning needs.

Use this endpoint to browse active regulations and their associated learning needs for a selected operating context. This endpoint supports compliance discovery; it does not determine whether a regulation applies to a particular organization or whether a learning object satisfies its requirements.

*Regulatory tags are provided for discovery and informational purposes only. Go1 does not provide legal, compliance, HR, financial, or professional advice and does not warrant that any content is current, complete, or aligned with applicable laws or regulations. Customers are responsible for assessing whether content is suitable for their own compliance needs.*

parameters.name: ids[]
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by regulation ID.

Send up to 50 `ids[]` values to return matching active regulations. IDs match the `id` field returned in each regulation response.

Example: `ids[]=reg_01M0VX0XC5ZEDBW5E28ZJQYDXP`

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description:
Searches active regulations by keyword.

The search applies text matching across regulation names and descriptions, and may also use semantic matching from the regulation search index. Use it for short keyword or natural-language queries.

Example: `keyword=OSHA`

parameters.name: facets[]
parameters.description:
Requests facet buckets for filterable regulation fields.

Supported values:
- `industries`
- `country_or_region`
- `state_provinces`
- `city_localities`
- `mandate_status`

Example: `facets[]=country_or_region`

parameters.name: industries[]
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by industry display value.

Send one or more `industries[]` values to return regulations associated with any of the supplied industries.

Example: `industries[]=Arts%2C%20Recreation%20and%20Entertainment`

enum: Administrative and Support and Waste Management
Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction
Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Electricity, Gas, Water and Waste Services

parameters.name: mandate_status
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by mandate classification.

Values:
- `required`: returns regulations marked as mandatory.
- `best_practice`: returns regulations marked as recommended best practice.

Example: `mandate_status=required`

parameters.name: country_or_region[]
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by country or region in their locations.

Use ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for countries or UN M49 codes for regions. Send one or more `country_or_region[]` values to return regulations for any supplied country or region.

Example: `country_or_region[]=US`

parameters.name: state_provinces[]
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by state or province in their locations.

Send one or more `state_provinces[]` values to return regulations for any supplied state or province.

Example: `state_provinces[]=California`

parameters.name: city_localities[]
parameters.description:
Filters regulations by city or locality in their locations.

Send one or more `city_localities[]` values to return regulations for any supplied city or locality.

Example: `city_localities[]=Chicago`

parameters.name: include[]
parameters.description:
Includes optional related data in each regulation.

Values:
- `topics`: includes topic relationships for each returned regulation.

If omitted, topic relationships are not returned.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of regulations to return per page. Must be between 1 and 50. Default is 20. The response `meta.total` value shows the total number of matching regulations before this page limit is applied.

parameters.name: use_scroll
parameters.description:
Activates "scrolling" mode to paginate through large result sets.

How it works:
- When `use_scroll=true` is set, the response includes a `meta.next_scroll_id` property in the body.
- This `next_scroll_id` value is valid for 5 minutes and is used to retrieve the next page of results.
- The number of results per page is determined by the `limit` parameter.

parameters.name: scroll_id
parameters.description:
The pointer to the next page of results, obtained from a previous scroll request.

Usage:
- Initial request: pass `use_scroll=true`, and store the value of `meta.next_scroll_id` from the response.
- Subsequent requests: pass `use_scroll=true&scroll_id={next_scroll_id}` where `{next_scroll_id}` is the value from the previous response.

Notes:
- Each `next_scroll_id` value is valid for 5 minutes.
- Requires `use_scroll=true`.

Errors:
- Returns 400 (Invalid request) for invalid or expired `scroll_id` values.

parameters.name: use_scroll
parameters.description:
Activates “scrolling” mode to paginate through large result sets.

As standard pagination with offset parameter is limited to 10,000 results, pass `use_scroll=true` along with `scroll_id` parameter to paginate beyond this limit.

How it works:
- When `use_scroll=true` is set, the response includes a `next_scroll_id` property in the body.
- This `next_scroll_id` is valid for 5 minutes and is used to retrieve the next page of results.
- The number of result per page is determined by the `limit` parameter.

parameters.name: scroll_id
parameters.description:
The pointer to the next page of results, obtained from a previous scroll request.

Usage:
- Initial request: pass `use_scroll=true`, and store the value of `next_scroll_id` property from the response.
- Subsequent requests: pass `use_scroll=true&scroll_id={next_scroll_id}` where `{next_scroll_id}` is the value from the previous response.

Notes:
- Each `next_scroll_id` value is valid for 5 minutes.
- Only works with `facets[]` query parameter on the first scroll request (i.e. `use_scroll=true`). All other `scroll_id` requests will not return any requested `facets[]`.

Errors:
- Returns 400 (Invalid request) for invalid `scroll_id` values.
- Returns 404 (Not found) for expired `scroll_id` values.

player_configuration.description: Player configuration settings, that can be enabled or disabled for each play link that is generated. These settings offer a way to alter the player UI and behaviour in various ways. Enabled config parameters will be added to the returned play link URL as query parameters.

recommendations.description: Whether to show or hide content recommendations in the player. Recommendations are displayed as a modal in the player after a learner completes the learning object. Set `recommendations=0` to hide and `recommendations=1` (default) to show.

title.description: Whether to show or hide the title of the learning object in the top header bar of the player (desktop view). Set `title=0` to hide and `title=1` (default) to show.

sidebar.description: A setting that determines how the sidebar will behave when loading the player. Set `sidebar=closed` to remove the sidebar completely, `sidebar=collapsed` to load the player with the sidebar in a collapsed state, `sidebar=open` (default) to load the player with the sidebar in an open state.

restart.description: A setting that determines whether the given user will be re-enrolled into the learning object when the player loads, causing any previous enrollment and content progression to be archived. Set `restart=1` to re-enroll the user, or `restart=0` (default) to not re-enroll the user, and use an existing enrollment if one is available.

exitAction.description: A setting that determines the behaviour of the exit button in the player. Set `exitAction=1` to remove the exit button from the player UI. Set `exitAction=2` to redirect the user to a specified `exitUrl` upon clicking the exit button, must include the `exitUrl` property. Set `exitAction=3` (default) to send the user back to the previous Go1 page.

exitUrl.description: A URL that the user is redirected to when they click the exit button in the player, must be used with the `exitAction=2` property.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description:
Number of items to skip before starting to return results.
Used for pagination. For example, with `limit=20` and `offset=20`, 
items 21-40 are returned.

**Limitation**: `limit` + `offset` cannot exceed 10,000.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum number of results to return per page.
Must be between 1 and 10000. Default is 100.

parameters.name: family_name
parameters.description:
Filter by family name (last name). Performs partial matching.
Case-insensitive search.

**Examples:**
• family_name=Smith

parameters.name: given_name
parameters.description:
Filter by given name (first name). Performs partial matching.
Case-insensitive search.

**Examples:**
• given_name=John

parameters.name: email
parameters.description:
Filter by email address. Performs partial matching.
Case-insensitive search.

**Examples:**
• email=john.doe@example.com

parameters.name: keyword
parameters.description:
Universal search across full name (given_name + family_name) OR email address.
Returns accounts where the search term matches any part of the user's 
full name or email. Useful for quick user lookup.

**Examples:**
• keyword=john.doe@example.com

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
Filter by legacy account IDs. Supports multiple values using array syntax.
Use: `id[]=123&id[]=456` for multiple IDs.

**Examples:**
• id[]=123&id[]=456

parameters.name: account_guid
parameters.description:
Filter by account GUIDs. Supports multiple values using array syntax.
Use: `account_guid[]=acc_...&account_guid[]=acc_...` for multiple GUIDs.

**Examples:**
• account_guid[]=acc_ABC&account_guid[]=acc_DEF

parameters.name: manager_guid
parameters.description:
Filter by manager GUIDs. Returns accounts that are managed by any of the specified managers.
Supports multiple values using array syntax.
Use: `manager_guid[]=acc_...&manager_guid[]=acc_...` for multiple GUIDs.

**Examples:**
• manager_guid[]=acc_ABC&manager_guid[]=acc_DEF

parameters.name: group_id
parameters.description:
Filter by group IDs. Returns accounts that are members of any of the specified groups.
Supports multiple values using array syntax.
Use: `group_id[]=123&group_id[]=456` for multiple IDs.

**Examples:**
• group_id[]=123&group_id[]=456

parameters.name: roles
parameters.description:
Filter by role GUIDs. Returns accounts that have any of the specified roles.
Supports multiple values using array syntax.

**Available role GUIDs:**
• Administrator: `rol_01G3PZS7NCBKB170TEP3CC2BBH`
• Learner: `rol_01G3PZS7NZ0CF95J340P55FSZH`
• Manager: `rol_01G3PZS7NZBW04V44QBM48PP0C`
• Content administrator: `rol_01G3PZS7NXC78RP57SG0EXD0Z5`

**Examples:**
• roles[]=rol_01G3PZS7NCBKB170TEP3CC2BBH&roles[]=rol_01G3PZS7NZ0CF95J340P55FSZH

parameters.name: standard_fields
parameters.description:
Filter by standard fields associated with user accounts.

**Field Rules:**
• `external_user_id` can be filtered multiple times
• All other standard fields can only be filtered once

**Examples:**
• `standard_fields.external_user_id[]=123A` - Find user with external_user_id = 123A
• `standard_fields.external_user_id[]=123A&standard_fields.external_user_id[]=456B` - Find users with either ID
• `standard_fields.department=Sales` - Find users in Sales department (partial match)

parameters.name: additional_fields
parameters.description:
Filter by additional/custom fields associated with user accounts.
Supports exact match filtering using array syntax.

**Examples:**
• `additional_fields.department[]=Engineering` - Find users in Engineering department
• `additional_fields.age[]=25` - Find users aged 25
• `additional_fields.employee_id[]=12345` - Find user with employee ID 12345

**Supported Operators:**
• `[]` - Exact match for strings and numbers
• `[min]`  will match all records greater than or equal to this date
• `[max]` will match all records less than or equal to this date.

parameters.name: include[]
parameters.description:
Specify which extended fields to include in the response.
By default, only basic account information is returned.

**Available Fields:**
• `standard_fields` - Include standard fields (external_user_id, department, etc.)
• `additional_fields` - Include custom/additional fields

**Examples:**
• `include[]=standard_fields.external_user_id&include[]=standard_fields.department`
• `include[]=additional_fields.colour`
• `include[]=additional_fields.colour&include[]=standard_fields.external_user_id`

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Filter by account status (active/inactive).
• `true` - Show only active users
• `false` - Show only inactive users
• Omit parameter - Show both active and inactive users

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sorts the results of your request by a given property.
Enum:
 - given_name
 - family_name
 - name
 - email
 - status
 - created_time
 - updated_time
 - logged_in_time
 - account_guid
 - _gc_user_id
 - _gc_user_account_id
 - standard_fields.*
 - additional_fields.*

**Examples:**
• sort=given_name,standard_fields.external_user_id,additional_fields.dob

parameters.name: order
parameters.description:
Orders the results by a given direction.
Enum:
 - asc
 - desc

**Examples:**
• order=asc,desc

parameters.name: created_time
parameters.description:
Filter user accounts by created time in ISO-8601 format.
 - [min]  will match all records greater than or equal to this date
 - [max] will match all records less than or equal to this date.

 Examples:
 - created_time[min]=2024-07-01 – Returns all user accounts created after July 1st, 2024
 - created_time[min]=2024-01-01&created_time[max]=2024-06-30 – Returns all user accounts created between January 1st, 2024 and June 30th, 2024
 - created_time[max]=2022-01-01 – Returns all user accounts that were created prior to January 1st, 2022

parameters.name: updated_time
parameters.description:
Filter user accounts by updated time in ISO-8601 format.
 - [min]  will match all records greater than or equal to this date
 - [max] will match all records less than or equal to this date.

 Examples:
 - updated_time[min]=2024-07-01 – Returns all user accounts updated after July 1st, 2024
 - updated_time[min]=2024-01-01&updated_time[max]=2024-06-30 – Returns all user accounts updated between January 1st, 2024 and June 30th, 2024
 - updated_time[max]=2022-01-01 – Returns all user accounts that were updated prior to January 1st, 2022

parameters.name: logged_in_time
parameters.description:
Filter user accounts by logged in time in ISO-8601 format.
 - [min]  will match all records greater than or equal to this date
 - [max] will match all records less than or equal to this date.

 Examples:
 - logged_in_time[min]=2024-07-01 – Returns all user accounts logged in after July 1st, 2024
 - logged_in_time[min]=2024-01-01&logged_in_time[max]=2024-06-30 – Returns all user accounts logged in between January 1st, 2024 and June 30th, 2024
 - logged_in_time[max]=2022-01-01 – Returns all user accounts that were logged in prior to January 1st, 2022

parameters.name: include_managers
parameters.description:
Include manager details in the response.
When set to `true`, the response will include detailed information about managers assigned to each user account.
When set to `false`, manager information will be excluded from the response.

**Default:** `true` (for backward compatibility)

**Examples:**
• `include_managers=true` - Include manager details.
• `include_managers=false` - Exclude manager details.

parameters.name: has_direct_reports
parameters.description:
Filter to include only managers who have at least one assigned learner.
When set to `true`, only returns managers who are actively managing other users.
This filter only applies to accounts with the manager role.

**Default:** `false`

**Examples:**
• `has_direct_reports=true` - Show only managers with learners.
• `has_direct_reports=false` - Show all managers (default).
